title: Introduce KMS lease-warranting and audit chainproof
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: a recent support incident (SUP-4123) exposed two risks: operator-initiated CMK usage without tight temporal scoping, and audit ingestion that lacked tamper-evident integrity markers across hops. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: (1) a KMS lease-warrant router that mints short-lived operator leases (warrants) for CMK operations and enforces operator identity + region affinity at the proxy layer; and (2) an audit chainproof generator that produces chained HMAC envelopes per request and surfaces integrity headers downstream so forwarders can detect injection or truncation. Design choices: operator warrants are GRPC-level tokens bound to service-account identity, TTL, and region claim; warrants are optional and enabled via helm flags for Dedicated/Private customers. The chainproof uses KMS-wrapped symmetric keys and rotates ephemeral signing keys per lease to avoid long-lived HMAC secrets. Rollout plan: disabled by default; staged canary enable in staging clusters followed by a 2-week canary in production; operators can opt-in per deployment via helm values. Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-2289) and threat model attached - [x] KMS router + warrant store implementation with unit tests - [x] chainproof generator + verifier integrated into audit forwarder - [x] helm chart toggles and migration notes - [x] smoke e2e against local KMS emulator - [x] security review sign-off

release_notes: Add optional KMS warrant routing (operator lease tokens) that bounds operator-initiated CMK usage to TTLs and regions, and add an opt-in audit chainproof feature that emits HMAC-chained integrity headers to detect tampering across the audit pipeline. Both features are disabled by default and can be enabled via Helm values 'enableWarrantRouting' and 'enableAuditChainproof'.
